title: VHPN Dispensing & Compliance Policy v3.0
document:
From: Elena Rostova, Director of Pharmacy Operations
To: All Pharmacy Site Managers, Lead Pharmacists, and Compliance Officers
Subject: Mandatory Review: Updated Dispensing, Financial, and Audit Policy (Effective Q2)
Date: April 12, 2024

Team,

Please review the attached policy excerpt in full. This document consolidates updates to our compounding waiver tracking, manufacturer rebate tier classifications, controlled substance return authorizations, and boundary resolution protocols. All site managers must acknowledge receipt and ensure staff training is completed by April 30, 2024. The compliance dashboard will begin validating transactions against these rules on May 1, 2024.

Best regards,
Elena Rostova
Director of Pharmacy Operations
Veridian Health Pharmacy Network

--- ATTACHMENT: VHPN DISPENSING & COMPLIANCE POLICY v3.0 ---

1. Purpose & Scope
This policy establishes standardized operating procedures for prescription dispensing workflows, financial threshold authorizations, and compliance tracking across all Veridian Health Pharmacy Network (VHPN) retail, institutional, and mail-order locations. It applies to all licensed pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, pharmacy managers, and regional directors involved in prescription verification, compounding, returns processing, and rebate reporting. Adherence ensures alignment with state board of pharmacy regulations, federal controlled substance guidelines, and manufacturer contract obligations. Deviations require written approval from the Chief Pharmacy Officer and must be logged in the central compliance repository within 24 hours.

2. Version Control & Effective Dates
Policy versions are governed by their stated effective dates. Version 1.0 was effective January 1, 2022. Version 2.0 was effective October 1, 2023. Version 3.0 is effective April 1, 2024. The version in force on the exact date and time a dispensing event, return transaction, or financial calculation occurs determines the applicable rules. Retroactive application of newer versions is strictly prohibited unless explicitly authorized in a signed addendum by the Chief Pharmacy Officer. Filing dates, audit completion dates, or managerial approval dates do not alter which version governs the underlying event.

3. Compounding Fee Waiver Limits
Pharmacists may waive the standard $15.00 compounding fee for patients demonstrating documented financial hardship. Each licensed pharmacy technician is permitted a maximum of 5 fee waivers per rolling twelve-month period. Waivers require a signed patient hardship form and verification that household income falls below 200% of the federal poverty level. Store managers may issue one override per calendar quarter if the patient is actively enrolled in a state pharmaceutical assistance program. Overrides do not reset the technician's personal counter but are tracked separately for audit purposes.

4. Manufacturer Rebate Tier Classification
Monthly manufacturer rebate eligibility is determined by the total number of tiered formulary units dispensed during the reporting month. The classification table is as follows:
- Tier A: 0 to 999 units (Rebate rate: 2.5%)
- Tier B: 1,000 to 1,999 units (Rebate rate: 4.0%)
- Tier C: 2,000 to 2,999 units (Rebate rate: 6.5%)
- Tier D: 3,000 or more units (Rebate rate: 9.0%)
Calculations are automated by the central pharmacy information system on the 28th of each month at 23:59 local time. Units dispensed after this cutoff are assigned to the subsequent month's reporting cycle. Partial fills and multi-pack quantities are counted by individual unit equivalent.

5. Controlled Substance Return Authorization
Returns of Schedule II through V medications to authorized distributors due to expiration, recall, or inventory correction require tiered authorization based on wholesale replacement value. Under Version 1.0, returns with a wholesale value up to $600.00 require only the dispensing pharmacist's digital signature. Returns exceeding $600.00 require dual authorization from the dispensing pharmacist and the store manager. Version 2.0 (effective October 1, 2023) revised the threshold to $850.00. Returns processed under the Emergency Recall Protocol bypass value thresholds entirely but mandate pharmacy director approval within 48 hours of initiation.

6. Waiver Event Qualification & Exclusions
For the purpose of tracking limits in Section 3, a waiver event is recorded when the dispensing software logs fee code WVR-01 against a unique prescription identifier. Each distinct NDC processed with this code counts as one event. Refills are counted as separate events. If a prescription is cancelled and re-verified within four hours using the same fee code, the system consolidates the transaction and counts it as a single event. Waivers applied to sterile compounding preparations, cytotoxic chemotherapy admixtures, or pediatric dose adjustments under 5 mL are explicitly excluded from the technician's rolling count and do not trigger limit enforcement.

7. Boundary Resolution & Threshold Application
This section governs how numeric thresholds, tier boundaries, and limit caps are applied across all policy sections. When a calculated monetary value, counted quantity, or unit volume falls exactly on a stated boundary or limit threshold, it is classified into the higher tier or deemed to exceed the limit. The sole exception applies to patient weight thresholds and income percentage qualifications, which remain inclusive of the lower category. All currency values are rounded to the nearest cent using standard half-up rounding. Unit counts are treated as integers; fractional units resulting from multi-pack splits are truncated downward before classification.

8. Window Calculation & Audit Trails
Rolling time windows referenced in this policy are calculated using a strict calendar-day backward count from the date of the current event. The window includes all days up to, but not including, the day exactly 365 days prior to the current event date. Events occurring on the exact 365-day anniversary are excluded from the count. The compliance system generates automated alerts when a technician reaches 80% of their allocated limit. Discrepancies between logged waiver events and actual fee adjustments trigger a Level 1 operational review. Three Level 1 reviews within a rolling twelve-month period mandate a Level 2 compliance audit and mandatory retraining for the site manager.

questions.case: Pharmacy technician Marcus Lin attempts to process a compounding fee waiver for a patient on March 15, 2024. The pharmacy system logs the following past waiver transactions for Lin: April 2, 2023 (standard topical cream); June 15, 2023 (standard oral suspension); August 20, 2023 (sterile IV antibiotic preparation); November 3, 2023 (standard eye drops, cancelled at 14:10 and re-verified at 16:45 on the same day); December 10, 2023 (standard transdermal patch); January 5, 2024 (standard oral liquid); February 28, 2024 (standard topical ointment). All transactions used fee code WVR-01. Lin is not enrolled in any state assistance program and no manager overrides were issued.
questions.question: How many compounding fee waivers does Marcus Lin have remaining under the policy limit for the March 15, 2024 transaction?

options.name: 0 waivers
options.description: The limit has already been reached or exceeded by prior valid events.

options.name: 1 waiver remaining
options.description: Four valid prior events exist within the tracking window.

options.name: 2 waivers remaining
options.description: Three valid prior events exist within the tracking window.

options.name: Cannot be determined from the document
options.description: Insufficient information to calculate the rolling window count.

questions.rationale: Section 3 sets a limit of 5 waivers per rolling twelve-month period. Section 8 defines the rolling window as 365 calendar days backward from the current event date, excluding the exact 365-day prior date. For March 15, 2024, the window runs from March 16, 2023 through March 14, 2024. The April 2, 2023 event falls outside this window. The remaining events (June 15, Aug 20, Nov 3, Dec 10, Jan 5, Feb 28) are inside the window. Section 6 excludes sterile compounding (Aug 20) from the count. Section 6 also states that cancellations re-verified within four hours count as one event (Nov 3 counts as 1). The valid events inside the window are June 15, Nov 3, Dec 10, Jan 5, and Feb 28, totaling exactly 5. Since the limit is 5, Lin has 0 waivers remaining for the March 15 transaction.

questions.case: The central pharmacy information system finalizes the monthly rebate calculation for the Oakridge retail location on May 28, 2024. The automated report shows that the location dispensed exactly 2,000 units of tiered formulary medications during the May 1 to May 28 reporting cycle. No units were dispensed after the 23:59 cutoff on May 28.
questions.question: Is the Oakridge location eligible for Tier C rebate classification for the May reporting month?

criteria.yes: The dispensed unit count meets or exceeds the Tier C lower boundary, and the boundary resolution rule assigns exact boundary values to the higher tier.
criteria.no: The dispensed unit count falls below the Tier C threshold, or boundary resolution assigns exact values to the lower tier.

questions.rationale: Section 4 defines Tier C as covering 2,000 to 2,999 units. The location dispensed exactly 2,000 units. Section 7 states that when a counted quantity falls exactly on a stated boundary, it is classified into the higher tier. Therefore, exactly 2,000 units is classified into Tier C, making the location eligible.

questions.case: On September 28, 2023, the Westview pharmacy initiates a controlled substance return to the distributor for a batch of expired Schedule III medications. The wholesale replacement value of the returned inventory is calculated at $700.00. The transaction is not part of an emergency recall. The dispensing pharmacist completes the digital authorization form on October 2, 2023, and the store manager reviews the paperwork on October 5, 2023.
questions.question: What level of authorization is required to complete this return transaction?

options.name: Dispensing Pharmacist only
options.description: The wholesale value falls within the single-signature threshold.

options.name: Dispensing Pharmacist and Store Manager
options.description: The wholesale value exceeds the single-signature threshold, requiring dual approval.

options.name: Pharmacy Director approval required
options.description: The transaction triggers emergency recall or director-level oversight rules.

options.name: Cannot be determined from the document
options.description: The policy does not specify authorization levels for this value range.

questions.rationale: Section 2 states that the version in force on the exact date the event occurs governs the action, regardless of filing or approval dates. The return event occurred on September 28, 2023. Version 2.0 did not take effect until October 1, 2023, so Version 1.0 applies. Section 5 specifies that under Version 1.0, returns up to $600 require only the pharmacist's signature, while returns exceeding $600 require dual authorization from the pharmacist and store manager. Since $700 exceeds $600, dual authorization is required.

title: Veridian Grand Hotel Group: Reservation Agent Onboarding Checklist
document:
1. Scope & Operational Precedence
This onboarding checklist governs all reservation activities for the Veridian Grand Hotel Group, effective October 1, 2024. It applies to Junior Agents, Senior Agents, Team Leads, and Compliance Officers. All staff must acknowledge receipt within 48 hours of hire. When procedural conflicts arise, the following hierarchy applies: Section 5 (Booking Modifications & Cancellations) prevails over Section 3 (Rate Plan Authorization) for any rate adjustments tied to cancellations made within 48 hours of check-in. All other sections hold equal weight, with the most specific clause overriding general statements. Checklist completion is mandatory before independent system access is granted. Agents must reference this document for all daily operational decisions.

2. System Access & Authentication Protocols
New hires receive temporary credentials valid for exactly 30 calendar days. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) must be configured within 24 hours of account creation. System access tiers are assigned based on role and guest profile status. Junior Agents operate under "Standard" access, while Senior Agents and staff managing verified high-value accounts operate under "Elevated" access. Temporary accounts automatically expire at 23:59 UTC on the 30th day unless converted to permanent status by the IT Security team. Failure to convert results in immediate session termination and requires re-initiation of the onboarding checklist. Access to the legacy "HeritageBook" interface is restricted to users who have passed the Section 8 certification.

3. Rate Plan Authorization & Overrides
Standard room rates may be applied by any authorized agent. Junior Agents may manually override standard rates up to a maximum of $350 per night. Senior Agents may override up to $550 per night. Any override exceeding $550 requires explicit written approval from a Team Lead. Corporate rate plans (CorpA and CorpB) carry fixed nightly caps: CorpA is capped at $400, and CorpB is capped at $450. Applying a rate that exceeds a corporate cap voids the corporate discount tier entirely. However, if an agent operating under "Elevated" access applies a rate between the corporate cap and $550, the corporate discount remains intact provided a Team Lead co-signs the reservation within two hours of creation. All rate overrides are logged in the audit trail and subject to monthly review.

4. Guest Profile Management & Compliance
Every new guest profile requires valid government-issued ID verification before booking confirmation. Lifetime spend tracking is automated. Guests accumulating over $5,000 in lifetime spend are automatically assigned "Platinum" status and granted "Elevated" system access for any agent handling their reservations. Platinum status confers complimentary late checkout until 14:00 local time, subject to housekeeping availability. If a guest profile is flagged for "Payment Review," all rate overrides and corporate discounts are suspended immediately, regardless of the handling agent's access tier or the guest's status. Payment Review flags are automatically cleared after 72 hours of verified payment activity. Agents must document the reason for any manual flag placement.

5. Booking Modifications & Cancellations
Cancellations submitted within 48 hours of the scheduled check-in time incur a standard penalty equal to 100% of the total booking value. This penalty is waived if the guest submits verified medical documentation. However, medical waivers are strictly prohibited for any reservation confirmed using a promotional code beginning with the prefix "FLASH". If a medical waiver is denied due to the "FLASH" prefix restriction, and the guest holds Platinum status, the cancellation penalty is automatically reduced to 50% of the total booking value. Promotional code bookings cannot be modified to change the room category or bed configuration. If a cancellation penalty is successfully waived, any pending rate adjustments under Section 3 are immediately nullified.

6. Commission & Partner Settlements
Commission structures are strictly segmented by booking channel. Online Travel Agency (OTA) partners receive a flat 15% commission on the net room rate. Direct bookings processed through the hotel portal or telephone center receive a 0% commission. When a booking is modified after initial confirmation, the commission percentage is recalculated based on the new total net rate, but the channel classification remains unchanged. Commission payouts are processed automatically on the 15th of each calendar month, covering all confirmed stays from the preceding month. If a booking is cancelled between the 8th and the 15th of any month, the associated commission is clawed back and deducted from the partner's next scheduled payout. Partners with negative balances after clawback are suspended from the partner portal until the balance is settled.

7. Escalation & Dispute Resolution
All guest or partner disputes regarding penalties, rate adjustments, or commission calculations must be logged in the central case management system within five business days of the incident. Team Leads are authorized to resolve financial disputes up to $500. Disputes exceeding $500 must be escalated to a Compliance Officer. If a dispute involves a guest with Platinum status, the case automatically bypasses the Team Lead queue and is routed directly to a Compliance Officer, regardless of the monetary value. Compliance Officers have final adjudication authority on all escalated matters. The standard resolution window is ten business days from case creation. Extensions require written approval from the Regional Director.

8. Training Completion & Certification
The onboarding checklist must be fully completed and signed off by both the HR Coordinator and the assigned Team Lead by the end of Day 14 of employment. Independent system access is contingent upon passing the mandatory operational certification exam by Day 21. The exam covers rate plan logic, cancellation policies, and compliance flags. Failure to achieve a passing score of 85% or higher by Day 21 results in immediate revocation of all system privileges. Recertification is required annually on the anniversary of the hire date. Agents who miss the annual recertification window by more than three business days must retake the initial onboarding checklist.

criteria.yes: The chain of rules (spend threshold -> access tier -> rate cap/override limit) mandates Team Lead co-signature or approval for the specified rate and plan.

questions.rationale: Section 4 states that a lifetime spend over $5,000 grants "Elevated" system access. Section 2 defines "Elevated" access as operating under Senior Agent rules. Section 3 states that Senior Agents may override up to $550, but CorpB has a fixed cap of $450. Overriding above the corporate cap requires Team Lead approval. Since $480 exceeds the $450 cap, Team Lead approval is mandatory.

title: Apex Logistics Fleet Operations Handbook: Chapter 4 - Vehicle Use & Compliance
document:
1. Scope & Definitions
This chapter governs the use, maintenance, and reporting of all vehicles registered under the Apex Logistics Fleet Program, effective January 15, 2024. Fleet assets are classified into three tiers: Class A (passenger sedans and compact hybrids), Class B (light utility trucks and cargo vans), and Class C (heavy haulers and specialized transport units). "Authorized Driver" refers to any employee with a valid commercial or standard driver’s license, a clean record for the preceding 36 months, and a signed Fleet Agreement on file. "Standard Operating Hours" are defined as Monday through Friday, 0600 to 1800 local time. All time limits, deadlines, and reporting windows referenced throughout this handbook exclude weekends and federal holidays, unless explicitly stated otherwise. Tenure calculations for eligibility purposes begin on the date of official onboarding, not the date of offer acceptance or initial training attendance. The Fleet Control Center operates 24/7 and serves as the primary point of contact for all emergency routing and incident coordination. Telematics data is audited monthly for compliance with geofencing and idle-time restrictions.

2. Vehicle Assignment & Eligibility
Assignment of fleet vehicles is strictly tied to role classification and tenure. Senior Logistics Coordinators become eligible for Class B vehicles after completing 18 months of continuous service. Field Sales Representatives qualify for Class A vehicles after six months. New hires may receive a provisional Class A assignment for a maximum of 30 calendar days pending completion of background verification and safety certification. Provisional assignments automatically terminate on the 31st day unless formally converted to permanent status by the Fleet Operations Manager. 

[Form V-IR Submission Guidelines]
All incidents requiring documentation must be logged using the Vehicle Incident Report (Form V-IR). The form must be submitted to the compliance portal within 24 hours of the event. If the incident involves a third-party commercial vehicle, the standard financial penalties and deductibles apply regardless of any training exemptions, promotional waivers, or internal safety drills that may otherwise be in effect. Drivers must attach police reports or third-party contact information when applicable. Failure to attach required documentation results in an automatic processing delay of five business days. Form routing requires supervisor digital signature before archival.

3. Fuel & Charging Protocols
Company-issued fuel cards are programmed with per-transaction limits to prevent unauthorized purchases. Class A vehicles are capped at $150 per fill-up, while Class B vehicles are capped at $250. Electric vehicles (EVs) must utilize internal depot charging stations during Standard Operating Hours. Exception: EV drivers may utilize public fast-charging networks when internal stations are at capacity, subject to a strict reimbursement cap of $40 per session. All public charging receipts must be uploaded to the expense portal within 72 hours. Refueling with a personal card requires prior written approval and is reimbursed at the base rate only. Lost or stolen fuel cards must be reported immediately; replacement cards carry a one-time $25 administrative fee. Public chargers must support CCS or CHAdeMO protocols to qualify for reimbursement.

4. Maintenance & Repairs
Preventative maintenance is scheduled automatically every 10,000 miles or every six months, whichever occurs first. Drivers must not authorize repairs exceeding $200 without direct approval from the Fleet Maintenance Supervisor. Unauthorized repairs void the manufacturer warranty and will be billed directly to the employee’s payroll. Exception: Emergency roadside repairs necessary for immediate safety or vehicle operability are pre-approved up to $300 per incident. If an emergency repair coincides with a scheduled maintenance window, the emergency repair takes precedence, and the routine service is deferred by exactly 14 calendar days. Tire replacements and brake pad services require a minimum of two competitive quotes before authorization. All warranty claims must be filed within 10 business days of service completion.

5. Accident & Damage Reporting
Any collision, theft, or structural damage must be reported immediately to the Fleet Control Center. Following initial notification, the driver must complete Form V-IR and submit it through the compliance portal. When damage estimates exceed $1,000, the corporate insurance policy triggers a driver deductible. The base deductible is set at $500 for Class A vehicles and $750 for Class B vehicles. Deductible calculations are final upon submission and cannot be appealed unless fraud or administrative error is proven. Towing services must be coordinated exclusively through Apex’s contracted provider, Roadside Assist Pro, to ensure coverage. Police reports are mandatory for incidents occurring on public roadways within municipal jurisdictions.

6. Mileage Tracking & Tolls
Odometer readings must be recorded in the telematics app at the start and end of every shift. Discrepancies exceeding 50 miles require a written explanation. Toll road usage is reimbursed automatically when the total charge per trip falls below $25. Charges of $25 or higher require a scanned receipt or digital pass tag statement. Exception: Cross-state tolls are reimbursed at 110% of the base rate to account for interstate administrative fees. Cross-state is defined as any single trip that crosses a recognized state border. 

Furthermore, regarding public EV charging exceptions outlined in Section 3: Unless the charge occurs after 2000 hours on a Saturday or Sunday, the $40 session cap remains strictly enforced. If the charge does occur after 2000 hours on a weekend, the $40 cap is waived entirely, provided the driver logs the transaction in the night-shift portal within one hour of completion. This weekend override applies regardless of internal station capacity. Night-shift portal access requires Level 2 security clearance. Reimbursement processing occurs bi-weekly on Fridays.

7. Policy Amendments & Superseding Directives
This handbook supersedes all prior fleet guidelines, memoranda, and verbal directives issued before January 15, 2024. However, specific operational adjustments may be issued during peak demand periods. The Q3 2024 Operational Memo, issued on August 12, 2024, explicitly overrides Section 5 regarding driver deductibles during certified safety training. The memo states: "During the month of September, any damage incurred while participating in a company-mandated defensive driving course or warehouse logistics drill shall have its driver deductible waived in full." This waiver applies to all vehicle classes and supersedes the base deductible amounts listed in the main policy. All amendments must be signed by the Director of Operations to take effect. Compliance audits for memo adherence are conducted quarterly.

8. Emergency Override & Executive Exemptions
C-Suite executives and Department Heads may bypass standard fuel and charging caps when mission-critical travel requires immediate action. This bypass requires the submission of Form F-9 (Executive Exemption Request) within 48 hours of the transaction. Form F-9 must include the vehicle VIN, transaction timestamp, amount, and business justification. Submissions received after the 48-hour window are automatically rejected and billed to the executive’s departmental budget. The 48-hour calculation follows the standard time-limit exclusions defined in Section 1. Rejected exemptions cannot be reinstated under any circumstances. Budget allocation codes must match the approved quarterly travel matrix.

questions.case: On Saturday, October 12, at 2115 hours, driver Elias Vance uses a public fast-charger for his Class A EV because the internal depot stations are full. The session costs $58. Vance logs the transaction in the night-shift portal at 2210 hours on the same day.
questions.question: What is the reimbursement outcome for Vance's charging session?

options.name: Cap waived, full reimbursement
options.description: The session cost is fully reimbursed because the weekend night override applies.

options.name: Capped at $40, partial reimbursement
options.description: The standard public charging cap applies, limiting reimbursement to $40.

options.name: Not eligible for reimbursement
options.description: The transaction fails portal logging requirements and is denied.

options.name: Requires Fleet Manager approval
options.description: The cost exceeds standard limits and needs manual authorization.

questions.rationale: Section 3 establishes the outer exception: public EV charging when internal stations are full is capped at $40. Section 6 contains the inner exception: unless the charge occurs after 2000 hours on a weekend, the $40 cap remains enforced; if it does occur after 2000 hours on a weekend, the cap is waived entirely provided the driver logs it in the night-shift portal within one hour. Vance charged at 2115 on Saturday (after 2000 on a weekend) and logged at 2210 (within one hour). Therefore, the inner clause triggers, waiving the $40 cap and allowing full reimbursement. The lure incorrectly applies the outer exception while ignoring the inner override in Section 6.

questions.case: On September 18, driver Mara Lin is operating a Class A vehicle during a company-mandated defensive driving course. She collides with a third-party commercial delivery truck. The damage estimate is $1,200. She submits Form V-IR with all required documentation.
questions.question: What financial responsibility applies to Lin following this incident?

options.name: Deductible waived in full
options.description: The training waiver overrides all standard penalties.

options.name: $500 deductible applies
options.description: The third-party commercial vehicle rule reinstates the base deductible.

options.name: $750 deductible applies
options.description: The Class B rate applies due to commercial vehicle involvement.

options.name: Cannot be determined from the document
options.description: Conflicting rules leave the outcome ambiguous.

questions.rationale: Section 5 sets the base Class A deductible at $500 for damage over $1,000. The Q3 2024 Memo in Section 7 supersedes Section 5, waiving deductibles for September training incidents. However, the Form V-IR Guidelines in Section 2 state that if an incident involves a third-party commercial vehicle, standard penalties apply regardless of training exemptions. Because Lin hit a commercial truck, the Form V-IR rule overrides the Memo's waiver, reinstating the Section 5 base deductible of $500. The lure incorrectly stops at the Memo's waiver without checking the Form's third-party override.

questions.case: On Friday, November 3, at 1700 hours, Chief Financial Officer David Chen uses his executive fuel card to bypass a standard cap for an urgent client visit. He submits Form F-9 on Monday, November 6, at 1900 hours.
questions.question: How is Chen's Form F-9 submission classified?

options.name: Compliant
options.description: The submission falls within the allowed window after accounting for standard exclusions.

options.name: Late
options.description: The submission exceeds the 48-hour limit and triggers budget billing.

options.name: Requires extension
options.description: Executive status mandates a separate approval process for weekend submissions.

options.name: Cannot be determined from the document
options.description: Missing information about holiday status prevents a ruling.

questions.rationale: Section 8 requires Form F-9 submission within 48 hours of the transaction. The case does not explicitly state whether weekends count toward this limit, which makes the deadline appear ambiguous. However, Section 1 explicitly defines that all time limits and reporting windows exclude weekends and federal holidays. Applying this definition, the 48-hour clock starts on Monday, making the Monday 1900 submission well within the compliant window. The lure incorrectly assumes a strict 48-hour calendar calculation ignoring the definition in Section 1.

title: ApexBuild Subcontractor Onboarding & Compliance Checklist
document:
1. Programme Scope & Effective Dates
This onboarding framework governs all Tier-2 and Tier-3 subcontractors engaged for structural framing, mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP), and façade installation across the Meridian Development portfolio. Onboarding is mandatory before any site mobilization, equipment delivery, or invoice submission. The Effective Contract Date for every subcontractor is calculated as exactly forty-five calendar days after the Central Procurement Office receives the fully executed Master Service Agreement (MSA). This date triggers the start of the billing cycle, insurance verification windows, and quarterly performance reviews. If the MSA is received on a weekend or public holiday, the receipt date defaults to the preceding business day. All calendar references follow the standard Gregorian calendar; leap years are accounted for in day-count calculations. Subcontractors failing to complete onboarding by the Effective Contract Date will be automatically suspended from the active vendor registry until compliance is restored.

2. Documentation Submission & Processing Windows
Subcontractors must submit a complete documentation package to the Vendor Compliance Portal. Required items include: (a) current business registration certificate, (b) state tax clearance letter issued within the last twelve months, (c) corporate W-9 form, and (d) signed code of conduct acknowledgment. The submission window closes on the fifteenth day of the month immediately preceding the planned mobilization date. Packages received after this cutoff are processed during the next available window, automatically delaying the Effective Contract Date by five business days per month of delay. Emergency call-out contracts may bypass the submission window if a written waiver is signed by the Regional Project Director and filed with Procurement within twenty-four hours of the emergency declaration. Incomplete packages are returned to the vendor with a deficiency notice; resubmission must occur within ten calendar days or the contract offer is revoked.

3. Insurance, Bonding & Risk Transfer
All onboarding subcontractors must maintain active Commercial General Liability (CGL) insurance with a minimum coverage of $2,000,000 per occurrence and $4,000,000 aggregate. Certificates of Insurance must name ApexBuild and all Meridian Development entities as additional insureds. Performance bonds are mandatory for any single contract exceeding $500,000 in total value. Bonds must be issued by a surety company rated A- or higher by Best’s Ratings. Verification of insurance and bonding documents must be completed no later than ten business days before site access credentials are issued. Failure to provide valid certificates by this deadline results in immediate revocation of site access until documentation is corrected. Hazardous materials handling contracts require an elevated CGL minimum of $5,000,000 per occurrence regardless of other thresholds.

4. Safety Compliance & Personnel Certification
Every site supervisor assigned to a Meridian project must hold a current NCCER Level 3 certification or an equivalent state-recognized structural safety credential. Certification must be verified through the National Safety Registry prior to badge issuance. Annual refresher training is mandatory for all supervisory personnel and must be completed by March 31 of each calendar year. Subcontractors must maintain a project-specific Safety Implementation Plan (SIP) that outlines fall protection protocols, heavy equipment operation zones, and emergency evacuation routes. The SIP must be stamped and approved by the Regional Structural Engineer before any concrete pouring or crane operations commence. Non-compliance with certification or SIP requirements triggers an automatic work stoppage order. Work may only resume after a joint inspection by ApexBuild Safety Officers and the subcontractor’s designated safety manager confirms full remediation.

5. Financial Qualification & Billing Priority
Subcontractors are evaluated on financial stability to determine billing priority and payment terms. The Financial Qualification Score is calculated using the formula: (Current Ratio × 100) + (Days Payable Outstanding ÷ 10). Subcontractors must submit an audited financial statement with their initial MSA package. A minimum Financial Qualification Score of 85 is required to qualify for Net-30 payment terms. Scores below 85 automatically assign Net-45 payment terms for the first twelve months of engagement. Financial scores are recalculated quarterly using the most recent submitted statements. Subcontractors whose scores drop below 80 will be placed on probationary billing status, requiring pre-approval for all purchase orders exceeding $25,000. Financial audits submitted after the Effective Contract Date must be received within fifteen calendar days to avoid a downgrade to Net-60 terms.

6. Capacity Assessment & Prime Slot Allocation
Prime assignment slots are allocated monthly on the first business day of each month. Allocation is based on the Capacity Index, calculated as: (Available Crew Hours ÷ Project Required Hours) × 100. Subcontractors must report available crew hours through the Resource Management Dashboard by the 25th of the preceding month. A Capacity Index of 110 or higher qualifies a subcontractor for prime assignment slots. Prime slots are limited to three per calendar quarter per trade discipline. Subcontractors with a Capacity Index below 110 are placed in the secondary queue and assigned only overflow or remedial work packages. Capacity assessments are frozen for thirty days following any major personnel turnover event reported by the subcontractor. The Project Controls Manager validates all capacity submissions against historical productivity data before finalizing the monthly allocation roster.

7. Performance Tracking & Exception Protocols
Quarterly performance reviews evaluate subcontractors on Defect Rate (DR) and On-Time Delivery (OTD). DR is calculated as (Number of Rework Incidents ÷ Total Work Packages) × 100. OTD is measured as the percentage of scheduled milestones completed by the agreed deadline. Subcontractors are classified into performance tiers based on DR:
- Tier 1: DR less than 0.40%
- Tier 2: DR from 0.40% to 1.20%
- Tier 3: DR greater than 1.20%
Performance reviews are conducted on the fifteenth day of the month following each fiscal quarter. An exception to the standard insurance requirements applies when a subcontractor maintains an OTD score of 98% or higher for two consecutive quarters. Under this exception, the mandatory CGL insurance minimum is reduced to $1,500,000 per occurrence, provided the active contract value remains below $750,000. This exception is automatically applied during the next insurance verification cycle and does not require separate approval. Subcontractors falling below the OTD threshold in any quarter revert immediately to standard insurance requirements.

8. Precedence Hierarchy & Boundary Definitions
When multiple evaluation metrics compete for limited resources or priority status, the following precedence rules apply. For prime slot allocation, if two or more subcontractors qualify, the entity with the higher Financial Qualification Score takes precedence. If Financial Qualification Scores are identical, the higher Capacity Index prevails. If both metrics are identical, seniority by original vendor registration date determines the winner. All numeric thresholds, boundaries, and percentage cutoffs referenced in this checklist are inclusive. Values falling exactly on a stated boundary qualify for the more favourable classification or requirement tier. In the event of a procedural conflict between sections, Section 8 overrides all other sections. Exception protocols documented in Section 7 override general requirements stated in Section 3. All disputes regarding checklist interpretation must be escalated to the Chief Procurement Officer, whose written determination is final.

questions.case: Subcontractor Alpha and Subcontractor Beta both apply for the sole available MEP prime assignment slot for the Q3 cycle. Alpha reports a Current Ratio of 1.75 and Days Payable Outstanding of 30. Alpha's available crew hours are 8,500 against a project requirement of 8,000 hours. Beta reports a Current Ratio of 1.60 and Days Payable Outstanding of 50. Beta's available crew hours are 9,200 against the same 8,000-hour project requirement. title: Aurion Logistics T&E Escalation Runbook
document:
1. Purpose & Governance
This runbook governs all travel and expense (T&E) escalations for Aurion Logistics. It applies to employees, contractors, and vendor representatives submitting claims via the SpendTrack portal. All escalations bypass standard manager approval when triggered by policy violations, missing receipts, or budget overruns. The T&E Steering Committee retains final authority on disputes exceeding $15,000. Department heads may not override tier routing once a trigger condition is met. All routing decisions are logged in the central compliance ledger with immutable timestamps. The Chief Financial Officer reviews monthly exception reports to ensure consistent application of these protocols across all business units.

2. Escalation Tiers & Routing
Tier 1 covers automated flags for claims under $2,500. These are resolved by Finance Operations within 48 hours. The Finance Operations team validates receipt authenticity and matches vendor codes against the approved supplier list before closing the ticket. Tier 2 covers claims between $2,500 and $10,000 requiring regional oversight. These route to the Regional Compliance Officer (RCO). Tier 3 covers claims above $10,000 or involving executive travel. These route to the VP of Finance. Tier 4 covers disputes involving legal holds or audit flags. These route to Internal Audit. Response SLAs are strict: Tier 1 (48h), Tier 2 (72h), Tier 3 (96h), Tier 4 (120h). The response clock starts upon ticket creation and pauses only for weekend holidays in the claimant’s home region. Ticket creation timestamps are recorded in UTC and converted to local time for SLA tracking.

3. Financial Thresholds & Approval Limits
Base approval limits follow the corporate matrix: Managers ($5,000), Directors ($15,000), VPs ($50,000). Escalated claims require dual sign-off when exceeding the submitter’s base limit by more than a defined percentage. Dual sign-off requires one finance approver and one legal representative. Claims flagged for vendor risk bypass matrix limits and automatically route to Tier 3 regardless of amount. For calculation purposes, the excess percentage is determined by dividing the claim amount by the base limit and subtracting one. Results must be precise to two decimal places. Currency conversions use the exchange rate published on the transaction date.

4. Version History & Effective Dates
This runbook incorporates three distinct artefacts: the Core T&E Policy (v1.0), the Q3 Compliance Memo, and the Standard Escalation Form. Version changes apply strictly based on the transaction date (date of expense incurrence), not the submission or approval date. v1.0 was effective from 1 Jan 2022 to 31 Aug 2023. During v1.0, dual sign-off triggered when exceeding the base limit by more than 30%. v2.0 was effective from 1 Sep 2023 to 31 Mar 2024. During v2.0, the threshold increased to 40%. v3.0 is effective from 1 Apr 2024 onward. During v3.0, the threshold increased to 50%. Historical claims processed under an older version retain that version’s rules permanently. All dates follow UTC midnight boundaries.

5. Priority Rules & Tie-Break Procedures
When multiple escalation triggers apply simultaneously, the following priority order determines routing: (1) Legal/Audit flags, (2) Vendor risk flags, (3) Amount-based thresholds, (4) Missing documentation. If a claim triggers both a vendor risk flag and an amount-based threshold, the vendor risk flag prevails and routes to Tier 3. If a claim triggers both a missing documentation flag and an amount-based threshold, calculate the excess percentage. If the excess percentage is strictly greater than the version threshold, the amount-based threshold prevails. Otherwise, the missing documentation flag prevails. For financial comparisons, exact percentages must be calculated to two decimal places. Rounding is not permitted for threshold determinations. When a calculated excess percentage exactly matches the version threshold, the claim does not trigger dual sign-off.

6. Supplemental Memo (Q3 2023)
Issued by the Director of Finance on 15 Aug 2023. This memo supersedes Section 3 regarding dual sign-off for contractor claims only. Contractor claims require dual sign-off when exceeding the submitter’s base limit by more than 25%, regardless of version history. This memo does not apply to full-time employees or vendor representatives. It remains in force until explicitly revoked. All contractor claims must also attach a signed service agreement to the escalation packet. The agreement must be dated on or before the transaction date to be valid.

7. Standard Escalation Form & Data Fields
All Tier 2 and Tier 3 escalations require a completed Form E-900. Mandatory fields include: Transaction Date, Claimant Role, Base Limit, Claim Amount, Trigger Type, and Receipt Status. The form calculates the excess percentage automatically. If the form’s calculated percentage conflicts with manual calculation, the manual calculation prevails. Form E-900 must be submitted within 5 business days of the trigger event. Failure to submit within this window defaults the claim to Tier 4. The form must reference the correct version number based on the transaction date. System validation rejects forms with mismatched version references.

8. Audit Trails & Documentation Requirements
Every escalation must retain a digital audit trail for 7 years. Supporting documents include original receipts, vendor contracts, and approval emails. Redacted documents are unacceptable for Tier 3 and Tier 4. If a receipt is missing but a vendor invoice exists, the claim may proceed at Tier 2 only if the invoice matches the claim amount exactly. Partial matches require Tier 3 routing. All Tier 3 and Tier 4 decisions require a written justification memo signed by the routing officer. Storage formats must be PDF/A to ensure long-term readability. Access controls restrict Tier 4 files to Internal Audit and the CFO. Retrieval requests require a written justification and supervisor approval.

The Director's base limit is $15,000 (Sec 3). The excess percentage is (21,000 / 15,000) - 1 = 0.40 or 40.00%. Section 5 explicitly states that when a calculated excess percentage exactly matches the version threshold, the claim does not trigger dual sign-off. Since 40.00% is not strictly greater than 40%, dual sign-off is not required.

questions.case: A Manager submits a claim for $7,490 incurred on 10 May 2024. The claim triggers both a missing documentation flag and an amount-based threshold. The Finance team calculates the excess percentage against the base limit.

Section 5 states that when missing documentation and amount-based thresholds conflict, the amount-based threshold prevails only if the excess percentage is strictly greater than the version threshold. Since 49.80% is not strictly greater than 50%, the amount-based threshold does not prevail.

Section 6 (the Q3 Compliance Memo) supersedes Section 3 for contractor claims, setting the dual sign-off threshold at >25% regardless of version history. The Manager's base limit is $5,000 (Sec 3). Since 40% exceeds the contractor-specific 25% threshold, dual sign-off is required. The lure traps readers who use the form's auto-calculated 38% or ignore the memo's override for contractors.

title: Oakhaven Municipal Planning Authority: Permit Rate Card & Administrative Bundle (2023-2024)
document:
1. Scope & Temporal Definitions
This document governs all municipal permit transactions processed by the Oakhaven Municipal Planning Authority (OMPA) between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2024. It applies to primary applicants, licensed contractors, and municipal liaisons. For all rate calculations, a "calendar quarter" is strictly defined as January 1 through March 31, April 1 through June 30, July 1 through September 30, and October 1 through December 31. Events submitted on the final day of a quarter are assigned to that quarter for all cumulative tracking purposes. The term "applicant" refers exclusively to the individual or entity holding the primary permit file number. Secondary contractors, subcontractors, and municipal liaisons are excluded from cumulative tracking and fee caps. All monetary values are in local currency and exclude applicable municipal taxes. Disputes regarding temporal boundaries must be resolved using the submission timestamp recorded in the central ledger.

2. Base Permit Fees & Classifications
Permit fees are categorized by project scope and structural classification. Residential Class A (single-family, under 2,500 sq ft) carries a base fee of $450. Residential Class B (multi-family or over 2,500 sq ft) carries a base fee of $780. Commercial Class I (retail, under 10,000 sq ft) carries a base fee of $1,200. Commercial Class II (industrial or over 10,000 sq ft) carries a base fee of $2,400. Projects designated as "Heritage-Protected" under Municipal Code 14-C qualify for a 15% reduction on the applicable base fee. This discount applies only to the base fee and does not extend to expedited surcharges, inspection fees, or penalty assessments. The discount is calculated after any municipal tax exemptions are applied but before administrative retention fees.

3. Expedited Processing & Quarterly Limits
Applicants may request expedited processing to reduce standard review times from forty-five business days to ten business days. An expedited request incurs a surcharge equal to twenty percent of the base permit fee. Each applicant is limited to two expedited requests per calendar quarter. This limit applies to new submissions, major amendments, and reinstatement requests. Requests that are withdrawn before the initial review stage still count toward the quarterly limit if the submission timestamp falls within the quarter. Requests that are rejected due to incomplete documentation are also counted. The quarterly counter resets automatically on the first day of each new quarter and cannot be carried forward or borrowed.

4. Payment, Refunds & Form Compliance
All permit fees must be paid via electronic transfer or municipal credit account within five business days of approval. Refunds for cancelled or withdrawn permits are processed within fourteen business days and are subject to a ten percent administrative retention fee. Any fee discount claimed on an initial submission must exactly match the "Project Classification" field on the attached Permit Application Form (Rev 4). If the form field specifies a different classification than the discount claimed, the discount is automatically voided, and the applicant is billed the full standard base fee. Payment disputes must be filed within thirty days of the invoice date; late disputes are dismissed without review. Form mismatches are flagged during automated validation and trigger an immediate billing adjustment.

5. Site Inspection & Compliance Surcharges
All Class A and Class B permits require a minimum of two site inspections. The base inspection fee is $250 per visit. Additional inspections requested by the applicant incur the same fee. If a site fails compliance during an inspection, a $150 compliance surcharge is applied per violation. Repeat violations on the same permit within a sixty-day window incur a compounded surcharge of $300 per violation. Inspection fees are non-refundable regardless of project status. Contractors must schedule inspections at least seventy-two hours in advance; same-day requests are denied unless a municipal emergency is declared by the Fire Marshal or Public Works Director.

6. Revision, Amendment & Penalty Protocols
Minor revisions (cosmetic changes, material substitutions) incur a flat fee of $75. Major revisions (structural changes, footprint alterations, use-case changes) incur a fee equal to fifty percent of the original base fee. If an applicant exceeds the quarterly expedited processing limit defined in Section 3, any additional expedited requests within that same quarter are processed at standard speed and incur a 50% administrative penalty on the base fee. These over-limit requests are not eligible for the standard expedited fee structure. Penalty fees are invoiced separately and must be paid within ten business days to avoid permit suspension. Appeals against penalty assessments must be submitted to the OMPA Review Board within fifteen days of the invoice date.

7. Administrative Memo (2023-10-15)
Issued by Director Eleanor Vance, this memo supersedes conflicting provisions in Section 2 regarding Heritage-Protected projects. Effective immediately, any Heritage-Protected project with an approved budget exceeding $500,000 shall receive a reduced discount of 5% on the base fee, rather than the standard 15%. This adjustment reflects updated municipal budget allocations for high-value heritage preservation. The memo explicitly overrides the base fee tables in Section 2 for qualifying projects but does not alter form compliance requirements, inspection protocols, or expedited processing limits. All pending applications are subject to this adjustment upon budget verification. Discrepancies between this memo and the base rate card are resolved in favor of the memo.

8. Effective Dates & Version Control
This document comprises the Standard Rate Card (Sections 1-6), the Director's Memo (Section 7), and the Application Form guidelines (referenced in Section 4). Version 2.0 was effective January 1, 2023. Version 2.1 was effective January 15, 2024. Version 2.1 updates the base inspection fee in Section 5 from $250 to $400 per visit. All permit transactions are governed by the version active on the date of the triggering event (submission, inspection, or violation), not the filing date, decision date, or payment date. Historical versions remain archived for audit purposes. Discrepancies between bundled artefacts are resolved by the precedence order: Memo > Rate Card > Form Guidelines.

questions.case: Applicant Marcus Thorne submitted expedited processing requests for three separate Commercial Class I permits on August 12, August 28, and September 29, 2024. All three requests passed the initial completeness check and were entered into the municipal tracking system within their respective submission dates.

criteria.yes: The applicant has submitted two or fewer qualifying expedited requests within the relevant calendar quarter window.
criteria.no: The applicant has submitted more than two qualifying expedited requests within the relevant calendar quarter window, triggering the over-limit penalty.

questions.rationale: Section 1 defines the calendar quarter as July 1 through September 30. Section 3 limits applicants to two expedited requests per calendar quarter and states that all requests passing completeness count toward the limit. Section 6 specifies that exceeding the quarterly limit triggers a 50% administrative penalty and removes eligibility for the standard expedited fee. With three qualifying requests in Q3, the limit is exceeded, making the answer no.

questions.case: Applicant Linnea Cross submitted a Heritage-Protected Commercial Class II permit application with an approved budget of $650,000. The initial submission claimed the standard heritage discount. The attached Permit Application Form (Rev 4) listed the Project Classification as "Commercial Class I" instead of "Commercial Class II". The municipal budget office verified the $650,000 figure on October 20, 2023.

criteria.no: The project fails to meet the discount criteria due to budget thresholds, memo supersession, or form classification mismatches.

questions.rationale: Section 2 grants a 15% heritage discount. Section 7 (Memo) supersedes Section 2 for projects over $500k, reducing the discount to 5%. Section 4 states that if the form's Project Classification field does not exactly match the discount claimed, the discount is automatically voided. Here, the budget exceeds $500k (triggering the 5% cap), and the form lists Class I instead of Class II (voiding the discount entirely). Therefore, the 15% discount is not qualified.

Since the inspection occurred on January 10, 2024, the pre-update $250 fee applies.

title: Meridian Health Partners Pharmacy Dispensing Pricing Schedule
document:
1. General Provisions & Definitions
This pricing schedule governs all retail pharmacy dispensing transactions processed under the Meridian Health Partners (MHP) network, effective 01 January 2024. All fees, surcharges, and rebates apply to claims adjudicated on or after this date. The term 'rolling window' refers to a continuously moving period calculated backward from the date of the current transaction. 'Standard unit' denotes a single prescription container or dose pack as defined by the National Drug Code. 'Satellite clinic' refers to any MHP-affiliated dispensing location operating under a primary pharmacy license but located more than 5 miles from the headquarters. All monetary values are in USD. Pricing adjustments are applied sequentially: base fee, then volume modifiers, then surcharges, then exemptions. Claims processed outside MHP network guidelines are billed at commercial list prices and are excluded from this schedule.

2. Base Dispensing Fees & Cost Tiers
Dispensing fees are calculated based on the daily drug cost (DDC) as reported by the manufacturer or wholesaler on the transaction date. The following tiered structure applies to all non-compounded, non-controlled medications:
- Tier A (DDC $0.01 to $4.99): $12.50 per container
- Tier B (DDC $5.00 to $14.99): $18.75 per container
- Tier C (DDC $15.00 to $29.99): $24.00 per container
- Tier D (DDC $30.00 and above): $32.50 per container
Prescriptions originating from physicians enrolled in the Chronic Care Initiative qualify for a 10% reduction on the base dispensing fee. Prescriptions from non-enrolled physicians are billed at standard tier rates. The Chronic Care Initiative enrollment status is verified at the point of claim submission and cannot be retroactively adjusted. Base fees are non-negotiable and apply regardless of patient copayment amounts or insurance network tier.

3. Compounding Protocols & Patient Caps
Compounded medications require prior batch authorization and are subject to strict volume controls to prevent therapeutic overlap and supply chain strain. Each compounded preparation carries a flat $45.00 compounding fee in addition to the applicable base tier fee. No patient may be dispensed more than 12 compounded topical or oral doses within any rolling 30-day period. This cap applies per patient medical record number, regardless of prescriber, pharmacy location, or diagnosis code. The rolling window resets daily based on the date of the most recent compounded dispense. If a transaction would cause the count to exceed 12 within the active window, the claim is automatically rejected at the pharmacy management system level. Exceptions to the cap require written approval from the MHP Clinical Pharmacy Director and are processed manually with a 72-hour turnaround. Compounded doses dispensed for veterinary use are exempt from all patient caps but incur a 25% environmental handling surcharge.

4. Controlled Substance Pricing & Age Adjustments
All Schedule II through V medications dispensed under this schedule attract a 12% regulatory compliance surcharge applied to the total base fee. This surcharge covers state board reporting, secure storage audits, and mandatory dispensing logs. The 12% surcharge is waived for patients under 18 years of age, reflecting federal pediatric access guidelines. The waiver applies only to the primary patient on the prescription; dependent children added to a parent's account must be billed individually. Controlled substances dispensed in liquid form incur an additional $8.50 measurement calibration fee. Schedule II drugs require dual-verification signatures from licensed pharmacists, but this operational requirement does not alter the pricing structure. All age determinations are based on the patient's date of birth relative to the transaction date, not the prescription write date.

5. After-Hours & Emergency Dispensing Surcharges
Pharmacy operating hours are classified as standard (08:00 to 18:00 Monday through Friday) and after-hours (18:00 to 08:00 Monday through Friday, plus all hours on Saturdays and Sundays). Any transaction processed during after-hours windows incurs a flat $15.00 administrative fee per claim. This fee compensates for reduced staffing and extended system monitoring. Emergency dispensing, defined as a prescription filled and handed to the patient within 120 minutes of the initial request timestamp, adds a 20% markup to the base dispensing fee. The emergency markup is calculated on the base fee before any surcharges or exemptions are applied. If a transaction qualifies for both after-hours and emergency status, both fees apply cumulatively. Emergency status must be flagged in the pharmacy dispensing software at the time of transaction; retroactive flagging is prohibited. After-hours fees do not apply to automated refill kiosks or mail-order shipments.

6. Exemption Validation & Processing Requirements
All pricing exemptions, waivers, and reductions require valid documentation submitted through the MHP Claims Gateway. The under-18 exemption referenced in Section 4.2 does not apply unless the dispensing pharmacy submits a Pediatric Verification Form within 24 hours of the transaction timestamp. Failure to submit the form within the 24-hour window results in automatic reversal of the exemption and assessment of the full 12% regulatory surcharge. Exemption validation is performed daily at 02:00 system time. Claims processed on Fridays, Saturdays, or Sundays must have the verification form submitted by 24:00 on the following Monday to maintain validity. The Chronic Care Initiative fee reduction described in Section 2.2 requires no additional form submission, as enrollment status is pulled directly from the provider registry. All exemption reversals trigger an audit flag and may result in temporary suspension of pharmacy network privileges if repeated three times within a calendar quarter.

7. Precedence, Boundary Resolution & Audits
Where multiple pricing rules overlap or conflict, the rule yielding the higher net charge to the payer prevails, except for patient safety waivers mandated by federal law. All numeric boundaries in pricing tables and tier classifications are inclusive of the lower threshold and exclusive of the upper threshold. For example, a value exactly matching a tier boundary falls into that tier or the next higher tier based on the inclusive/exclusive rule stated herein. Quarterly pricing audits are conducted by the MHP Finance Department on the first business day of January, April, July, and October. Discrepancies identified during audits are billed at the originally claimed rate unless the pharmacy can produce contemporaneous documentation proving error. All pricing schedule amendments require 30 days written notice to participating pharmacies. This document supersedes all prior dispensing rate agreements, verbal commitments, and regional addendums issued before 01 January 2024.

questions.case: A patient with medical record number MHP-8842 received compounded topical doses on the following dates: 05 Nov, 08 Nov, 11 Nov, 14 Nov, 17 Nov, 20 Nov, 23 Nov, 26 Nov, 29 Nov, 02 Dec, 05 Dec, 08 Dec, and 11 Dec. The pharmacy attempts to process a new compounded topical dose for the same patient on 11 December 2024.
questions.question: Is the pharmacy permitted to dispense this new compounded dose under the standard patient cap?

criteria.yes: The total number of compounded doses dispensed within the rolling 30-day window ending on the transaction date is 12 or fewer.
criteria.no: The total number of compounded doses dispensed within the rolling 30-day window ending on the transaction date exceeds 12.

questions.rationale: Section 3.3 caps compounded doses at 12 within any rolling 30-day period per patient. Section 1 defines the rolling window as calculated backward from the current transaction date. The transaction date is 11 Dec. The 30-day window runs from 12 Nov to 11 Dec inclusive. Doses within this window are: 14 Nov, 17 Nov, 20 Nov, 23 Nov, 26 Nov, 29 Nov, 02 Dec, 05 Dec, 08 Dec, 11 Dec. That is 10 doses. Wait, I need it to exceed 12. Let me recount. Actually, 12 Nov to 11 Dec is 30 days. Dates in window: 14,17,20,23,26,29 Nov (6) + 2,5,8,11 Dec (4) = 10. That's under 12. I need to adjust the case dates to ensure it crosses 12. Let's change the case dates to: 01 Nov, 04 Nov, 07 Nov, 10 Nov, 13 Nov, 16 Nov, 19 Nov, 22 Nov, 25 Nov, 28 Nov, 01 Dec, 04 Dec, 07 Dec. Transaction on 10 Dec. Window: 11 Nov to 10 Dec.
